text: Ladies and gentlemen, in addition to what my colleague and friend, Mr. Colin McCarthy,
has told you about the phenomenon of UFOs over Australia, I would like to add a few things.
First of all, I would like to mention the so-called Ballarat Conference in February
65, just exactly two years ago.
It was a conference held by all the groups in Australia in a town of Ballarat in Victoria.
The conference was sponsored by the Astronomical Society of Ballarat and was attended by the
scientific consultant of the Royal Australian Air Force.
It was a momentous event in the history of UFO groups in Australia.
It began with a number of people giving their sightings and drawing the objects they saw
on the blackboard, and other very reliable observers, such as Father Gill, of whom you
have heard from my colleague, Mr. McCarthy.
Now, when the first part of the conference was completed, we invited the Air Force man,
Mr. Roberts, to comment and to express his opinion about the phenomenon of UFOs, particularly
in Australia.
In the course of one hour and twenty minutes, Mr. Roberts was explaining to us the way sightings should be recorded.
He has given us the questionnaire that the Air Force used and this went on for one hour
and twenty minutes until we were really bored.
And one of his last sentences was something like this, well I don't think you have any
facts at all.
then a gentleman in the second row got up and he says with all due respect for your position as the scientific consultant of the Air Force
and your scientific knowledge I think you are wrong
because many reliable people like Father Gil and myself have seen objects which cannot, could not
be identified, planes, meteors or any other known phenomena. And he said I should know because during
during the last war, I was the air marshal of your air force.
Well, you can imagine what happened to the scientific consultant. Frankly, he was buried six foot deep.
Six foot deep, exactly. And ever since then, we thought that we had no trouble from those quarters.
But there is one more faction of society which had to be tackled, and we prepared for that for approximately 12 months.
It was a prominent academic body, the University of Sydney.
Since the president of our group, UFO Investigation Center in Sydney, is Dr. Lindner, a truly
brilliant man, a gold medalist of the Bologna University and a postgraduate of Sydney University,
we decided that he was the right man to go, as you and I might say, into a lion's den.
Then he announced to his colleagues in the university that he had an important and interesting lecture which he wanted to deliver before the top professors of the university.
and in November 1965, the lecture was held at the Sydney University
and attended by 40 professors and tutors of the Sydney University.
No students, no outsiders.
The lecture was supposed to last only 45 minutes.
It went on for two hours and twenty, and nobody was bored.
There were many questions. Dr. Lindner produced considerable amounts of evidence, which we accumulated in the course of many, many years.
At the end of the lecture, I wouldn't like to name this professor, one of the top scientists in Australia.
he came up to Dr. Lentner, patted him on the shoulder, and said,
This is one of the most interesting and the most provoking lectures I ever had in my long life.
Well, so that was our second victory.
So, what I am trying to prove is this.
Ever since 1953, our main policy was that we should make ourselves convincing to those
who hold the reins of government and those who control our minds, these scientists.
and I feel that we have succeeded in this assignment in Australia.
At the present moment, we have a very fine reputation as an organization
and as a magazine, a publication on this particular subject,
and we are quite popular with most television stations and radio stations in Australia.
Now, this is merely a proof to you that if qualified men with the right policy tackle
a certain subject, they are liable to get somewhere.
Now, I would like to make a few remarks of a rather general character.
I have just completed a world tour.
I went right around Australia to Singapore to Bombay. From Bombay I went on to Madras,
Kolkata and then I finished up in Darjeeling almost on Tibetan border. From there I went
back to... I lived in India for two months then I went on to Europe. I passed through Egypt,
Egypt, Sicily, Italy and many countries of Europe. I'm saying this with a view of stressing
one very important point that UFOs are not confined to any one country or continent.
They are a global phenomenon.
Now, I don't like to use the word UFOs myself.
I think a fraction of these UFOs are what I call IFOs, or identified flying objects.
Neither myself nor any scientist is particularly interested in photographs or reports about meteors or planes or anything that is of more or less conventional nature.

But a small fraction of all these strange sightings, photographs and motion pictures, some of them classified, like my colleague has mentioned to you, and I have myself have seen one, the so-called Port Moresby film, which is now in the security headquarters in Melbourne.
I was just lucky to see it before it became classified.
It was a question of about two weeks between the time it was taken and the time it disappeared in certain quarters.
Now, all this evidence is very important.
And, as I say, a certain percentage of these sightings, of these photographs, of these motion pictures cannot be explained.
Undoubtedly, they are records of possible spaceships, possible visitations from other worlds.
There's a mass of evidence to prove that.
In view of that, I think that the subject which you and I are studying here deserves
the attention of serious scientists.
As you know, many scientists are now convinced that about 40% of all solar systems in the
universe have planets.
I interviewed the famous professor Hermann Oberth in Germany about seven months ago.
His opinion is even less reserved. He believes that it could be as much as 50% of all the stars in the Universe could have families of planets.
Now, of course, a very small fraction of, a very small percentage of these planets could
be inhabited by the different forms of life.
Not necessarily the one we know.
The basis of life may not be the same as it's on this Earth.
But we should not close our minds to the possibility that there are thousands, even millions of inhabited planets.
But that does not necessarily mean that they have followed exactly the same path of evolution as we have.
Now, in regard to skepticism as to emanating from some scientists that there could be no life on certain planets,

My main message tonight concerns the eventual contact
between this civilization X coming from some other world and ourselves.
How will that affect us?
In my opinion, if another civilization in the Universe makes contact with us,
and if their culture is much higher, then our economics, politics, ideology and traditions
will become obsolete overnight.
The attitude towards this planetary revolution, as I call it, should not be emotional but intellectual.
The nations of today have fought two horrible wars in this century alone. Ethics and humanism,
the prerequisites of any truly superior civilization, are absent. America has produced what has
been called by one of her thinkers the fun culture. And are we not following it today?
On this background of contemporary life, a sudden appearance of superior beings,
superior in technology, sociology and ethics could introduce a new age on this planet,
but only when the present system goes away. And perhaps this is the true meaning of space
visitations which are taking place today. Thank you.
